ablation.protocol: Same authored camera traces, 640x400, 8 samples/frame, 128 reference samples, 32 frames, same metric/threshold code. Only copied-app denoising shader stage bypasses differ. Raw/reconstruction within each run share traced samples. Separate runs retain tiny floating-point/AS variation.

diagnosis: The strongest evidence is the interaction: both spatial-only and temporal-only improve image and temporal error, while their original combination fails image error.

MetalRenderer passes temporally accumulated radiance into three spatial passes. Previously spatialFilter used only current SPP for blend strength and overwrote temporal history alpha with depth. At 8 SPP the blend remained 0.5 in every pass even on compatible 32-frame histories.

Neighborhood variance contains both noise and real illumination contrast; broad luma tolerance and same-plane/albedo compatibility can mix real shadow edges. Temporal accumulation already reduces noise, making repeated full-strength filtering unnecessarily biased.
Spatial results are not fed into temporal history; the temporal history texture is retained before the three spatial passes. No erroneous spatial feedback loop was found.

Primary guides describe pixel-center material, plane, normal and albedo, not direct-light visibility. Water normals are procedural, but the lake region is improved in the failing frame; no guide-generation change is justified by this evidence.

MotionValidation compares paired raw/reconstruction against independent references with matched camera and scene time. It measures display-space RGB error and temporal error differences after warmup. No metric mismatch or need to weaken its thresholds was found.

fixReasoning.change: Preserve accepted center-pixel history count in every spatial output alpha; reduce spatial strength using 8/(currentSPP*clamp(historyCount,1,32)+8).
fixReasoning.whyScoped: Keeps existing geometry/albedo/coverage rejection and all three filter passes. Newly revealed, reset, reactive and through-glass pixels retain count 1 and the existing fresh-frame strength. Stable accepted history receives less redundant smoothing.
fixReasoning.alphaContract: Presentation reads only RGB and explicitly writes opaque alpha. Spatial output has its own normal/depth guide and no production consumer needing its previous depth alpha. Count remains center-local, not blurred across neighbors.
fixReasoning.statisticalLimit: Accepted frame count is a bounded confidence heuristic, not an exact independent-sample count; temporal reprojection correlates samples. Targeted and full cross-location tests remain necessary.

testAlphaAudit.authorizedTestChange: Only those five bypass checks (dark joint, analytic sky, subpixel spire, emitter window, mixed distant window) now assert exact x/y/z equality plus a separate exact filtered.w == history.w confidence assertion. No numeric tolerances, camera traces, thresholds or other fixtures were changed.
testAlphaAudit.cpuValidation: swiftc -typecheck scripts/validate-denoiser.swift passed; no GPU execution was performed by this reviewer.
testAlphaAudit.otherFixtures: Adler raw/output coverage checks already use RGB. Its full-RGBA legacy-policy comparisons compare two shaders with identical new alpha semantics. Paired-motion and Metal presentation checks correctly require final display alpha 255, which presentation still supplies.

limits: Strong-edge regions still include Monte Carlo reference error and subpixel coverage; they locate bias but do not independently prove its mathematical cause.
Only two targeted cases were ablated here; other locations, quality presets, longer histories and exported movies require their own final regression records.

interpretation: The original shader also fails image error on the expanded world, so the failure cannot be attributed to the new confidence policy.

Spatial-only also fails image error; temporal-only gives exactly equal displayed raw and reconstructed error and temporal residual. The coarse-night history bypass makes temporal confidence irrelevant to this case.
The temporal-only run correctly exits1 under the unchanged strict-improvement test because equality is not improvement; it is an informative ablation rather than a passed renderer configuration.

correctedReasoning: The initial suggestion that32frames overstated independence was a general conservative-policy rationale, not an established explanation for Willis. The original/spatial-only/temporal-only ablations supersede that hypothesis for this case.

The existing coarse-night visible-emitter guard inspects a fixed radius2 neighborhood, whereas the three active spatial kernels reach radii2,4,8. Later passes can filter neighbors outside the protected current-coverage area.

Root is evaluating a guard radius of2*activeStep, preserving the first pass and existing geometry/material policies. This is a stencil-consistency correction, not a location-specific bypass or changed threshold.

Cumulative three-pass radiance support can reach14pixels. Matching the active radius alone is not a mathematical guarantee against every possible mixed-coverage halo. The final focused fixture actually exercises coarse-night dark-center coverage throughout each active support, including outer rings/corners, and catches the old radius2 guard; all33real-scene traces pass.
